subject: Transportation Systems
title: Airport Capacity Limits
description: A quick, practical guide to Airport Capacity Limits.

hook.text: Heathrow handles 1,300 flights daily on just two runways. It's at absolute maximum capacity.

buildup.text: A plane lands or takes off every 45 seconds. There's no room for a single extra flight.

discovery.text: Adding runways is nearly impossible at major urban airports—neighbors, politics, and cost block expansion.

twist.text: Some airports solve it by building offshore or on reclaimed land. Osaka's Kansai sits on an artificial island.

climax.text: Slot allocation at congested airports is worth millions. Landing rights at Heathrow trade like real estate.

punchline.text: The scarcest resource in aviation is asphalt.

quiz.question: Why can't major urban airports simply add more runways?
options: Space, noise regulations, politics, and costs block expansion
